top_choice_rationale: P001 (B002: Chetty, Hendren, Friedman) is the strongest on identification quality and checkability. It created a new empirical object, intergenerational mobility measured by place on population administrative records, and its mover and childhood-exposure designs separate place effects from sorting. A citation limited to measurement and exposure-based designs does not rest on the contested long-run causal claims. The margin over P002 (Kiyotaki-Moore) is narrow. P002 has a longer record and the cleanest attribution but weaker direct identification, and a maturity-heavy weighting could reverse the order. P003 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) is mature with concentrated credit, but its cross-country identification is weaker. P004 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) has the longest record but the most contestable three-name cut from an eight-name field. I rank an award above no award. P001's main costs are its short record, with core results from about 2014 to 2022, and the unresolved Katz-versus-Friedman seat, which rests on my unverified recollection that Katz co-authored the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis.
recusal_note: My profile shows no co-authorship or institutional tie to Chetty, Hendren, Friedman or Katz, nor to the credited names in P002, P003 or P004. I am a frequent co-author of Per Krusell (secretary, P004 supporter) and John Hassler (chair, P002 supporter). Their views are not independent of mine and I did not treat them as corroboration. I also have a long collaboration with Aghion, Bergeaud, Klenow and Li, none of whom are credited on these proposals. Disclosure only, not adjudicated.
